additional_concerns: The offer-level candidates node.968dbccb08282a4e8a580ae5 and node.bca408c75cbf8467afafada6 permit an unsupported prohibition result when the offer has a qualifying promotional connection but the counted gift does not; the binding notes acknowledge this issue but do not implement the missing same-component relationship.

Node.97af37a2579f59b0ee43211f adds an SFC-authorised-fund condition to the promoted product; the circular's distributor definition supplies actor context but does not expressly narrow the quoted paragraph 3.11 wording to that product category.

Node.142f34016b300f5c110eb249 is supported on its express definition that the provider offers the component; mapping provider to a funder or fulfiller who did not make the offer would change that meaning and lose the required actor attribution.

Entailment of claim.345e3fde4b1e95315df29ecd for node.bca408c75cbf8467afafada6 concerns preservation of conditional gift classification only, not implementation of professional classification or validation of its complete offer-level prohibition test.

The control plan refers to a stated source interval and competing temporal interpretations, but the supplied source text establishes no operative interval; the date of the referenced FAQ is not an effective-date rule, and these checks do not establish temporal applicability beyond the retained text.

TRUE_IS_PROHIBITED is supported here as the selected Code of Conduct 'should not offer' control, and TRUE_IS_COMPLIANT as satisfaction of that control alone; neither establishes a section 103 offence or compliance with the separate advertising requirements.

The structured.classification control cites the section 103 public-invitation offence rather than the classification qualification in db43e253bea18.u8.1651; that contextual evidence assignment does not establish structured-product classification and has not been imported into the required gift checks.
